title: Synonymous Recoding Reveals Gene-Caller Sensitivity in Short-Read Microbial Protein Thermometry
content: Inferring environmental conditions from microbial metagenomes often requires predicting proteins from short reads. Such inference may depend on the upstream gene caller even when encoded protein sequences are unchanged. Four bacterial or archaeal chromosomes were subjected to matched synonymous donor-profile recodings or codon-count-preserving within-gene permutations; the intended translations of corresponding 150-nucleotide fragments were verified as identical. Prodigal and FragGeneScan were compared using an established amino-acid-composition thermometer and 3,000 gene-cluster bootstrap resamples. Across 40 exploratory contrasts, the effects varied by genome, recoding mode and caller. In Thermotoga maritima, three FragGeneScan codon-order permutations shifted estimated temperature by +1.74 to +2.70 °C, despite very small shifts in overall fragment GC. Separately, five public paired-end metagenomic libraries from three studies showed consistently lower FragGeneScan than Prodigal estimates across three FragGeneScan models; however, the study-level two-sided sign-test result was p = 0.25. These results demonstrate conditional computational sensitivity, not a validated difference in actual environmental temperature.
